title: Subjuntivo con conjunciones temporales: cuando, hasta que, antes de que

sections.content: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, no matter the tense. Hasta que takes the subjunctive when the event was still pending at the reference point (esperaban hasta que el gobierno respondiera -- they were waiting for a response that hadn't come yet). Cuando, by contrast, takes the indicative when it introduces a real, completed past event (cuando el gobierno decidió...) -- the same conjunction family, but only some of them force uncertainty into the mood. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Estas ideas encontraron eco entre los trabajadores, hasta que se convirtieron en organización sindical concreta.
items.english: These ideas found an echo among the workers, until they turned into concrete union organization.

items.spanish: Esperaban allí, pacíficamente, hasta que el gobierno respondiera a sus peticiones.
items.english: They waited there, peacefully, until the government would respond to their demands.

items.spanish: El conflicto no hizo más que intensificarse antes de que terminara la década.
items.english: The conflict only intensified before the decade ended.

items.spanish: Nunca se estableció una cifra exacta antes de que el hecho quedara, durante décadas, prácticamente silenciado.
items.english: An exact figure was never established before the event remained, for decades, practically silenced.

sections.content: Watch the difference between the first hasta que example (se convirtieron, indicative -- reporting what actually, eventually happened) and the second (respondiera, subjunctive -- describing what the workers were waiting for, still uncertain at that moment in the story).
